Hi Lena — thanks, and great questions. High level answer up front: we deliver a signed bundle (tar) containing the image(s) + a canonical manifest JSON and a detached signature from an HSM-backed key (Redwood KMS/HSM). Below are the concrete items and the on-site verification steps. I've attached a sample signed manifest and checksums.

What we deliver (artifact bundle):
- signed-bundle.tar.gz (containing images/containers and the bundle manifest)
- rdw-signed-manifest.json (manifest with fields: bundle_id, model_id, versions, sha256 checksums, generated_at, expires_at, signers[])
- signer-roster.csv (who signed, key ids, HSM signer reference)
- crc32-checksums.txt (quick operator verification)

Signature model and verification:
- Signatures are generated by our HSM-backed KMS. We produce a detached ASN.1/PKCS7 signature and a human-readable verification script.
- On-site verification commands (example):
  1) sha256sum -c rdw-signed-manifest.json.checksums
  2) ./rdw-verify-signature --manifest rdw-signed-manifest.json --signature rdw-signed-manifest.sig --trusted-keys signer-roster.csv
  3) ./rdw-verify-policy --manifest rdw-signed-manifest.json --ttl-check

Acceptance & rollback windows:
- Recommended acceptance slot: 3–4 hours for smoke + integration tests. We can support your 4-hour slot.
- Recommended rollback window: 2–6 hours depending on staged steps; we typically plan for a 24-hour safe rollback policy if operator cadence allows.

Operator responsibilities (on-site):
- Verify checksums and signature before any install.
- Perform staging deploy to a non-production standby rack and run the smoke checklist (see attached PDF).
- Operator to take signed receipt (two-person rule) and update chain-of-custody spreadsheet.

Evidence package for auditors:
- Signed manifest, signer-roster.csv, courier manifest (signed by Redwood logistics), operator-acceptance-checklist.pdf with operator initials, and audit log export (we can provide a CSV of verification events).

Attachments sent: rdw-signed-manifest.json, signer-roster.csv, crc32-checksums.txt.

Questions for you:
- Confirm preferred acceptance window (dates/times).
- Do you require the signature to be in a specific format for your auditors (PKCS7 vs. CMS vs. JWS)? We support PKCS7 and JWS outputs.

If helpful, we can run a short dry-run signature verification with your security engineers over a screenshare.

Thanks,

Hi Lena — adding a few operational specifics from our side that ops and your facilities team will want to confirm:

Transport & handoff expectations:
- We require a sealed courier receipt signed by two Redwood reps and two on-site custodians at handoff. Courier manifest (digital) is included in the evidence package.
- Physical media is serialized and tamper-evident; operator should validate seal integrity prior to ingest.

On-site acceptance checklist (what to run during the 3–4 hour slot):
1) Unpack media, record serials, verify seals.
2) Run sha256 checksums against rdw-signed-manifest.json.checksums.
3) Run rdw-verify-signature and rdw-verify-policy (ensure expires_at > now).
4) Staged boot on non-prod rack, run smoke tests (health endpoints, model KV cache warm, sample inference latency within expected bounds).
5) Operator records results in operator-acceptance-checklist.pdf and returns scanned copy.

Operator training & followups:
- We can provide a 45-minute operator walkthrough 3 business days prior to the window.
- If you have alternate custodians, please send names and PII for courier pre-clearance.

I've attached the operator-acceptance-checklist.pdf for your change ticket. We will also include commander-level rollback steps that an on-site operator can execute without remote intervention.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Program Manager, Deployments

Quick internal note — capturing the final items we should include in the runbook before we send to Acme:

1) Verifier tool chain: include rdw-verify-signature (PKCS7 + JWS), rdw-verify-policy (TTL and key-revocation checks), and an offline verifier wrapper that outputs a single exit code and a machine-readable JSON pass/fail.
2) Expiration policy: manifests must include expires_at; our verifier will fail install if expires_at < now OR if any signer key appears on the revocation list. For emergency hotfixes we support time-limited one-off signatures but those require exec sign-off and an emergency courier.
3) Fallback policy: if verification fails during acceptance and signature is invalid, operator follows the rollback checklist and notifies Redwood on-call. We will also publish an audit CSV for all verification attempts.
4) SLA & rollback: propose we lock a 24-hour safe rollback window in contract language; during that time Redwood will prioritize support and can provide signed hotfixes if needed.

I'll prepare a short runbook doc (single page + checklist) and a Google Drive link to an example verifier binary and sample logs. We should send to Acme once Karthik approves the wording on signature formats.

-jb
Jordan Blake
Deployments Lead, Redwood Inference
